John of Brienne King of Jerusalem
RagShortTexts: The House of Brienne produced crusader sovereigns who ascended the thrones of Jerusalem and.

Variants.Content: A Champagne county family, the Briennes won wide chivalric renown across the crusader states. John of Brienne became King of Jerusalem by marriage in 1210, and in his eighties he was acclaimed co-Emperor of Constantinople, defending the city against Greek and Bulgarian armies. Later Brienne claims to the Duchy of Athens kept a Frankish lordship in Greece alive for another generation. The family's ties to Capetian and Scottish royalty made them a truly international dynasty. Their knights fought at Damietta and in Italy, and the Brienne name carried weight wherever Latin lords met.

The Briennes intermarried with Capetian and Scottish royal houses. Their commanders moved between Champagne, Italy, and the Levant as crusade and dynastic affairs required. Each marriage brought a dowry of castles or a promised county, so every alliance also meant a claim on land somewhere else.

Crusaders in the Damietta campaign of 1218-1219 waded through Nile mud under the Brienne banner, which John led in the fighting around the city. Troubadour songs remembered the charges through the dust. Soldiers who fought under such a banner expected pay in silver and a place in the front rank, and they often drew lots to decide who carried the standard into battle.
